A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCG and FuzzEval research despite the changed title. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–N are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 and Appendix M report original code-generation experiments measuring FDR-CE, selection efficiency, and pass@1 across models, datasets, and programming languages.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix M and adds comparisons with existing code-generation methods and a DeepSeek-R1 threshold sweep.

M1.justification: Fuzzing-based entailment estimation, adaptive unit-test sizing, confidence scoring, and threshold selection remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. Applying SCG to additional generation pipelines does not introduce a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: The same source benchmarks, algorithmic tasks, programming languages, and HumanEval+/MBPP+ evaluations are retained. The new '-f' names identify the fuzzing-based datasets already described in v1. Table 2 changes model and subset settings within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with CodeT, LDB, and SFS in Table 2, reporting each with and without SCG. This substantially broadens comparison beyond v1's four SCG-related baselines, which remain in the corresponding existing experiments.

E3.justification: The added Table 2 uses GPT-3.5-Turbo, alpha=0.4, epsilon_E=0.01, dataset-specific risk targets, full HumanEval-f, and a union of released MBPP subsets. Table 4 adds DeepSeek-R1 risk targets from 0.15 to 0.30. Existing evaluation metrics, splits, and default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends risk-threshold sensitivity analysis to DeepSeek-R1, while Table 2 examines the effect of adding SCG to established generation pipelines. Existing scoring-function, unit-test, parameter-sensitivity, and qualitative analyses—including Appendix M—are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 random calibration/test splits, the same percentile-whisker convention, and plus/minus summaries in tables. No changed run count, seed policy, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test is documented. Revised plus/minus values are concrete result changes.

E6.justification: v2 adds the pipeline comparisons in Table 2 and DeepSeek-R1 results in Table 4. It also revises SCG-EM's 1-PASS@1 values under retained settings: APPS changes from 0.840±0.352 to 0.020±0.098, with revisions across the other datasets and languages. Existing SCG scores and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the risk definitions and bounds, Theorem 1, Algorithms 1–2, and the arguments in Appendices H–K retain their mathematical content. The preliminary decomposition lemma moves to Appendix B, and lemma numbering changes. The new historical discussion does not alter the entailment definition.

C1.justification: v1 claims to introduce code entailment first. v2's introduction and conclusion narrow that novelty claim, acknowledge earlier programming-language literature, and identify the selective-generation learning algorithm as the main contribution. The central FDR-control and FuzzEval claims remain.

C2.justification: New Section 4.2.3 interprets the comparisons as demonstrating compatibility with post-filtering methods and reinforcement-learning-based generators, distinguishing SCG's risk control from accuracy improvement. The existing limitations concerning model quality, calibration, and distribution shifts are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete repository link for the code and evaluation dataset, whereas v1 only announces their release. Existing pseudocode, preprocessing descriptions, hardware information, and parameter-selection guidance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 situates code entailment relative to Massalin's probabilistic testing and differential/program-equivalence testing. Appendix A substantially revises the discussion of fine-tuning, ranking, and post-filtering methods, explaining SCG's complementary role and adding numerous relevant works.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, the introduction and extended related work are substantially recast, and the main preliminary section is consolidated into Appendix B. A new comparison subsection changes the results narrative, although most method and technical-appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2 and 4, groups Figures 2 and 3 earlier in the document, and changes headings, headers, typography, and some captions. The plotted figures themselves and most existing table structures are retained; subsequent tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves comparative relevance through CodeT/LDB/SFS evaluations and gives the contribution more credible positioning by acknowledging prior probabilistic testing. However, several new comparisons obtain low error with very low selection efficiency—for example, 0.002 for LDB+SCG on MBPP-f—limiting their practical implications. These additions support a limited overall quality gain while the core method, theory, and most evidence remain unchanged.
